source.text: מַשָּׂ֤א דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַדְרָ֔ךְ וְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק מְנֻחָת֑וֹ כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ עֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְכֹ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Oracle. [The] word of Yahweh [is] against [the] land of Hadrach, and Damascus [is] its resting place; for to Yahweh [is the] eye of humankind and all [the] tribes of Israel,

en.L: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] against the land of Hadrach, \q and Damascus [is] its resting place; \q for to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs the] eye on humankind \q and on all the tribes of Israel,
en.B: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is against the land of Hadrach, \q and Damascus is where it will come to rest; \q for the eye of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is on all humankind \q and on all the tribes of Israel,
en.R: This is a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is against the land of Hadrach, \q and it will come down on the city of Damascus. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over all people, \q and over all the tribes of Israel too.

fr.L: Oracle. La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [est] contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et Damas [est] son lieu de repos ; \q car {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} [appartient] l’œil sur l’humanité \q et sur toutes les tribus d’Israël,
fr.B: Oracle. La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et c’est sur Damas qu’elle se posera ; \q car l’œil {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est sur toute l’humanité \q et sur toutes les tribus d’Israël,
fr.R: Voici un message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il est contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et il va tomber sur la ville de Damas. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} surveille tous les êtres humains, \q et aussi toutes les tribus d’Israël.

es.L: Oráculo. La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [está] contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y Damasco [es] su lugar de reposo; \q porque {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} [pertenece el] ojo sobre la humanidad \q y sobre todas las tribus de Israel,
es.B: Oráculo. La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y en Damasco vendrá a reposar; \q porque los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} están sobre toda la humanidad \q y sobre todas las tribus de Israel,
es.R: Este es un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Es contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y caerá sobre la ciudad de Damasco. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vigila a toda la gente \q y también a todas las tribus de Israel.

vi.L: Sấm ngôn. Lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [nghịch cùng] xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và Đa-mách [là] nơi nó dừng lại; \q vì mắt của loài người và của mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên \q [đều hướng] về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}},
vi.B: Sấm ngôn. Lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghịch cùng xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và sẽ dừng lại trên Đa-mách; \q vì mắt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đoái xem cả loài người \q và mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Sứ điệp này nghịch cùng xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và sẽ giáng xuống trên thành Đa-mách. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đoái xem mọi người, \q và cả mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên nữa.

sw.L: Unabii. Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [li] juu ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q na Dameski [ni] mahali pake pa kupumzika; \q kwa maana kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] jicho juu ya wanadamu \q na juu ya makabila yote ya Israeli,
sw.B: Unabii. Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni dhidi ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q na Dameski ndipo litakapotua; \q kwa maana jicho la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} liko juu ya wanadamu wote \q na juu ya makabila yote ya Israeli,
sw.R: Huu ni ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ni dhidi ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q nao utaushukia mji wa Dameski. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawaangalia watu wote, \q na makabila yote ya Israeli pia.

ko.L: 신탁. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 하드락 땅에 [임하고], \q 다메섹이 그 [말씀이] 머물 곳이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 사람에게 [향한] 눈이 있고 \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파에게도 [있기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 신탁. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 하드락 땅을 치고, \q 다메섹에 내려 머물 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이 모든 사람을 지켜보시고 \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파를 지켜보시기 때문이다.
ko.R: 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 말씀이다. 이 말씀은 하드락 땅을 치고, \q 다메섹 성에 내릴 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 모든 사람을 지켜보시고, \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파도 지켜보신다.

pt.L: Oráculo: a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} [está] contra a terra de Hadraque, \q e Damasco [é] o seu lugar de repouso; \q porque {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} [pertence o] olho sobre a humanidade \q e sobre todas as tribos de Israel,
pt.B: Mensagem: a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está contra a terra de Hadraque, \q e é sobre Damasco que ela vai pousar; \q porque o olho {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está sobre toda a humanidade \q e sobre todas as tribos de Israel,
pt.R: Esta é uma mensagem {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Ela é contra a terra de Hadraque, \q e vai cair sobre a cidade de Damasco. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vigia todas as pessoas \q e também todas as tribos de Israel.

decisions.choice: oracle: the heading of a new part of the book (chapters 9-11), as again at 12:1
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-8 are dated to the reign of Darius and tell of Zechariah's visions and sermons. Chapters 9-14 have no dates and no visions. They fall into two parts, each headed with the same words, "An oracle. The word of the LORD" (9:1; 12:1); Malachi 1:1 opens with the same heading. The word for "oracle" comes from the verb "lift up". It is a solemn pronouncement from God, often a word of judgment on a nation, as in the oracles on the nations in Isaiah 13-23. Most of chapters 9-10 are poetry.

decisions.choice: Hadrach and Damascus: the land of Aram (Syria), north of Israel
decisions.reason: Hadrach is named only here in the Bible. It is usually identified with a city and region in northern Syria, near Hamath, that Assyrian records call Hatarikka. Damascus was the chief city of Aram. The oracle begins in the far north and moves south through Hamath (verse 2), along the coast through Tyre and Sidon (verses 2-4), to the cities of the Philistines (verses 5-7): the lands on Israel's borders that had long been its enemies.

decisions.choice: Damascus is its resting place: the word of the LORD will settle on Damascus
decisions.reason: The word of judgment is pictured as something that goes out and comes to rest on a place, as a load is set down. The same noun is used of the LORD's resting place in Zion (Psalm 132:14). The point is that the word will not pass Damascus by.

decisions.choice: to the LORD belongs the eye on humankind: the LORD watches over all people, Israel included
alternatives: the eyes of all people and of all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD
the eye of Aram belongs to the LORD (a change of one letter)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "for to the LORD [is the] eye of humankind and all the tribes of Israel". It is read here as saying that the LORD keeps watch over all the nations as well as over Israel, so that what happens to the cities named is his doing. It can also be read the other way round: the eyes of all people, and of all Israel's tribes, are turned toward the LORD as they see what he does. A small change to one letter of the word for "humankind" gives "Aram" (Syria), and some read "for the eye (or "the chief city") of Aram belongs to the LORD, as do all the tribes of Israel". The written Hebrew is translated here.

decisions.choice: An oracle (L, B); a message from the LORD (R); comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: Massa' is "oracle" at Literal and Balanced and "message" at Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced says "where it will come to rest" for "its resting place". Readable names Damascus as a city and says plainly what the eye of the LORD means (m4). The sentence runs on into verse 2, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

decisions.choice: massa "Oracle" (L, B), "Voici un message du SEIGNEUR" (R)
decisions.reason: The heading as the term sheet and published Isaiah 13:1 and Nahum 1:1; here there is no "concernant", since the Hebrew names no subject before "the word of the LORD".

decisions.choice: Chapters 9-14 are oracles: speech at every level, present and future, passé composé for the past; Zion, Jerusalem, Tyre and the other cities addressed or described as women are feminine
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for oracles and personified places.

decisions.choice: "Oráculo" (L, B); "Este es un mensaje del SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: Massa as a heading follows the Spanish prophets at each level; it opens the second part of the book, as again at 12:1.

decisions.choice: "Hadrac", "Damasco"
decisions.reason: Damasco is the published form; Hadrac is spelled as Spanish spells such names.

decisions.choice: "Unabii" (L, B); "ujumbe" (R) for massa'
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for an oracle heading, as the published Isaiah 13:1 and Nahum 1:1. Here the Hebrew has no "concerning X", so the word stands alone.

decisions.choice: "Hadraki"
decisions.reason: A new name, formed by the usual Swahili pattern (final vowel added after a closed syllable).

decisions.choice: "신탁" (L, B); "…께서 주신 말씀" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheets' word for massa' (oracle), recorded once for Zechariah 9-14 and Malachi. Each verse closes as its own Korean sentence, though the English runs on with a comma.

decisions.choice: Line breaks placed for Korean word order
decisions.reason: Korean is verb-final, so the clause about the LORD's eye is split before its last phrase rather than at the English break; each level keeps four lines as the English does.

decisions.choice: massa' "Sấm ngôn" (L, B) / "sứ điệp" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for an oracle heading, as Isaiah and 2 Kings 9:25.

decisions.choice: L reads "mắt của loài người ... [đều hướng] về CHÚA", one of the two readings the meaning decision allows; B and R follow the English, the LORD's eye on all people
alternatives: "vì CHÚA có mắt trên loài người" at L
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot keep the Hebrew's ambiguous "to the LORD the eye of humankind" without choosing; L keeps the Hebrew's order and the other reading, which the footnote names.

decisions.choice: Oráculo (L); Mensagem (B); Esta é uma mensagem (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 12:1): massa' takes the heading wording Isaiah 13:1 sets in Portuguese for the prophets, "oráculo" at Literal and "mensagem" at Balanced and Readable, with the colon Malachi 1:1 uses for the same heading, "Oráculo: a palavra do SENHOR".

decisions.choice: Hadraque; Damasco
decisions.reason: The unknown city (m2) is written as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Hadraque", with the vowel Portuguese adds after a final consonant, as in "Baruque"; Damascus is "Damasco", as the shared rules for the prophets set it.

source.text: וְגַם־חֲמָ֖ת תִּגְבָּל־בָּ֑הּ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן כִּ֥י חָֽכְמָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: and also Hamath [which] borders on it, Tyre and Sidon, for it is very wise.

en.L: and also Hamath, which borders on it, \q Tyre and Sidon, for she [is] very wise.
en.B: and on Hamath too, which borders it, \q and on Tyre and Sidon, wise as they think they are.
en.R: It is also against the city of Hamath, near Damascus, \q and against Tyre and Sidon, even though they think they are very wise.

fr.L: et aussi Hamath, qui la touche, \q Tyr et Sidon, car elle [est] très sage.
fr.B: et sur Hamath aussi, sa voisine, \q et sur Tyr et Sidon, si sages qu’elles se croient.
fr.R: Il est aussi contre la ville de Hamath, près de Damas, \q et contre Tyr et Sidon, même si elles se croient très sages.

es.L: y también Hamat, que limita con ella, \q Tiro y Sidón, porque ella [es] muy sabia.
es.B: y también sobre Hamat, que limita con ella, \q y sobre Tiro y Sidón, por más sabias que se crean.
es.R: También es contra la ciudad de Hamat, cerca de Damasco, \q y contra Tiro y Sidón, aunque se creen muy sabias.

vi.L: và cũng [nghịch cùng] Ha-mát, là [xứ] giáp ranh với nó, \q Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, vì nó rất khôn ngoan.
vi.B: và cũng nghịch cùng Ha-mát, xứ giáp ranh với nó, \q cùng Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, dù chúng tự cho mình là khôn ngoan.
vi.R: Sứ điệp cũng nghịch cùng thành Ha-mát ở gần Đa-mách, \q và nghịch cùng Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, dù chúng nghĩ mình rất khôn ngoan.

sw.L: na pia Hamathi, inayopakana nayo, \q Tiro na Sidoni, kwa maana [ni] wenye hekima sana.
sw.B: na juu ya Hamathi pia, inayopakana nayo, \q na juu ya Tiro na Sidoni, ingawa wanajiona kuwa na hekima nyingi.
sw.R: Ni dhidi ya mji wa Hamathi pia, ulio karibu na Dameski, \q na dhidi ya Tiro na Sidoni, ingawa wanadhani kwamba wana hekima sana.

ko.L: 그 땅과 경계를 맞댄 하맛에도, \q 매우 지혜롭다는 두로와 시돈에도 [임할 것이다].
ko.B: 그 말씀은 그 땅과 맞닿은 하맛에도 내리고, \q 스스로 지혜롭다고 여기는 두로와 시돈에도 내릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그 말씀은 다메섹 가까이 있는 하맛 성에도 내릴 것이다. \q 스스로 아주 지혜롭다고 생각하는 두로와 시돈에도 내릴 것이다.

pt.L: e também Hamate, que faz fronteira com ela, \q Tiro e Sidom, porque ela [é] muito sábia.
pt.B: e sobre Hamate também, que faz fronteira com ela, \q e sobre Tiro e Sidom, tão sábias como se julgam.
pt.R: Ela também é contra a cidade de Hamate, perto de Damasco, \q e contra Tiro e Sidom, mesmo que elas se achem muito sábias.

decisions.choice: Hamath, Tyre and Sidon: a Syrian city to the north, and the two great Phoenician ports on the coast
decisions.reason: Hamath stood on the Orontes river, north of Damascus. Tyre and Sidon were the chief cities of Phoenicia, on the coast north of Israel, rich from trade by sea. The word of judgment moves from Syria to the coast.

decisions.choice: for she is very wise: said with irony of Tyre's cleverness in trade
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular, so it speaks of Tyre in the first place, with Sidon beside it. Ezekiel 28:3-5 mocks the king of Tyre as "wiser than Daniel", a wisdom that had made him rich and proud. The next verse shows what that wisdom had built; verse 4 shows that it will not save the city. The word "for" may also be read "though": though she is very wise.

decisions.choice: and on ... too (B); It is also against (R); wise as they think they are (B); even though they think they are very wise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable carry on the sense of verse 1, that the word is against these places. They bring out the irony of "very wise" (m2) by saying that the cities think themselves wise, and they speak of Tyre and Sidon together.

decisions.choice: "por más sabias que se crean" (B); "aunque se creen muy sabias" (R)
decisions.reason: The praise of Tyre's wisdom is ironic, as the meaning decision reads it; B and R make the irony plain, as the English does. Hamat, Tiro and Sidón are the published forms.

decisions.choice: "kwa maana [ni] wenye hekima sana" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "she is very wise" refers to Tyre; Swahili verbs show no gender, and Literal brackets the copula. Balanced and Readable make the irony plain, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Hamate; Tiro; Sidom
decisions.reason: The cities (m1) take the forms Jeremiah 49:23 and the shared rules for the prophets give them in Portuguese, "Hamate", "Tiro", "Sidom".

source.text: וַתִּ֥בֶן צֹ֛ר מָצ֖וֹר לָ֑הּ וַתִּצְבָּר־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וְחָר֖וּץ כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And built Tyre a fortress for herself, and heaped up silver like dust, and gold like [the] mud of [the] streets.

en.L: And Tyre built herself a fortress, \q and heaped up silver like dust \q and fine gold like the mud of [the] streets.
en.B: Tyre has built herself a fortress; \q she has piled up silver like dust, \q and gold like mud in the streets.
en.R: The city of Tyre built strong walls to protect itself. \q It piled up silver as if it were dust, \q and gold as if it were mud in the streets.

fr.L: Et Tyr s’est bâti une forteresse, \q et elle a amassé l’argent comme la poussière \q et l’or fin comme la boue des rues.
fr.B: Tyr s’est bâti une forteresse ; \q elle a entassé l’argent comme la poussière, \q et l’or comme la boue des rues.
fr.R: La ville de Tyr a construit des murs solides pour se protéger. \q Elle a entassé l’argent comme si c’était de la poussière, \q et l’or comme si c’était de la boue dans les rues.

es.L: Y Tiro se edificó una fortaleza, \q y amontonó plata como polvo, \q y oro fino como el lodo de [las] calles.
es.B: Tiro se ha construido una fortaleza; \q ha amontonado plata como polvo \q y oro como lodo de las calles.
es.R: La ciudad de Tiro levantó murallas fuertes para protegerse. \q Amontonó plata como si fuera polvo, \q y oro como si fuera lodo de las calles.

vi.L: Ty-rơ đã xây cho mình một đồn lũy, \q chất bạc lên như bụi, \q và vàng ròng như bùn [ngoài] đường.
vi.B: Ty-rơ đã xây cho mình một đồn lũy; \q nó chất bạc như bụi đất, \q và vàng như bùn ngoài đường phố.
vi.R: Thành Ty-rơ đã xây tường lũy kiên cố để tự vệ. \q Nó chất bạc thành đống như thể bạc là bụi đất, \q và vàng như thể vàng là bùn ngoài đường.

sw.L: Naye Tiro amejijengea ngome, \q akarundika fedha kama mavumbi \q na dhahabu safi kama matope ya njiani.
sw.B: Tiro amejijengea ngome; \q amelundika fedha kama mavumbi, \q na dhahabu kama matope barabarani.
sw.R: Mji wa Tiro ulijenga kuta imara za kujilinda. \q Ulirundika fedha kana kwamba ni mavumbi, \q na dhahabu kana kwamba ni matope barabarani.

ko.L: 두로가 자기를 위하여 요새를 쌓고, \q 은을 티끌같이, \q 순금을 거리의 진흙같이 쌓아 올렸다.
ko.B: 두로는 자기를 위하여 요새를 쌓았다. \q 은을 먼지처럼 쌓아 두고, \q 금을 거리의 진흙처럼 쌓아 두었다.
ko.R: 두로 성은 자기를 지키려고 튼튼한 성벽을 쌓았다. \q 은을 먼지처럼 많이 쌓아 두었고, \q 금을 거리의 진흙처럼 많이 쌓아 두었다.

pt.L: E Tiro edificou para si uma fortaleza, \q e amontoou prata como pó \q e ouro fino como a lama das ruas.
pt.B: Tiro construiu para si uma fortaleza; \q amontoou prata como pó \q e ouro como lama nas ruas.
pt.R: A cidade de Tiro construiu muralhas fortes para se proteger. \q Ela juntou prata como se fosse pó, \q e ouro como se fosse lama das ruas.

decisions.choice: Tyre built a fortress: a play on the city's name
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name Tyre (Tsor) means "rock", and the word for "fortress" (matsor) sounds almost the same. Tyre stood on a rocky island just off the coast, protected by the sea and by high walls, and it held out against long sieges by Assyria and by Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 26-29). It was famous for being hard to take.

decisions.choice: silver like dust, gold like the mud of the streets: wealth beyond counting
decisions.reason: Dust and street mud are what is most common and least valued. Tyre's trade had made silver and gold as common as dirt; 1 Kings 10:27 says the same of silver in Solomon's Jerusalem. Ezekiel 27 lists the riches that came to Tyre by sea. The word used for gold is a poetic word for fine gold.

decisions.choice: The city of Tyre; strong walls to protect itself (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tyre is a city and that its fortress was its walls, and uses "it" for the city where the Hebrew speaks of it as "she".

decisions.choice: "Tyr s'est bâti une forteresse" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The wordplay on Tyre's name (tsor, matsor) that the meaning decision notes cannot be kept in French; the decision's note carries it.

decisions.choice: "두로", "두로 성" and "자기" for the city; never "그녀"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures Tyre as a woman; Korean repeats the name or uses "그 성", as the term sheet asks, and the play between Tyre (tsor) and fortress (matsor) is left to the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: a city is "nó" in the third person
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "nàng" for Zion and the women of Ezekiel; a foreign city under judgment is "nó". The pun on Tyre's name (Tsor, matsor) cannot be kept in Vietnamese; the meaning decision gives it.

source.text: הִנֵּ֤ה אֲדֹנָי֙ יֽוֹרִשֶׁ֔נָּה וְהִכָּ֥ה בַיָּ֖ם חֵילָ֑הּ וְהִ֖יא בָּאֵ֥שׁ תֵּאָכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, [the] Lord will dispossess her, and he will strike into the sea her strength, and she by fire will be consumed.

en.L: Look, the Lord will dispossess her \q and strike her strength into the sea, \q and she will be consumed by fire.
en.B: But look, the Lord will strip her of all she has \q and hurl her power down into the sea, \q and she will be burned up with fire.
en.R: But the Lord will take away everything she owns. \q He will throw her power into the sea, \q and the city will be burned to the ground.

fr.L: Voici, le Seigneur la dépossédera \q et frappera sa puissance dans la mer, \q et elle sera dévorée par le feu.
fr.B: Mais voici que le Seigneur va la dépouiller de tout \q et précipiter sa puissance dans la mer, \q et elle sera consumée par le feu.
fr.R: Mais le Seigneur va lui prendre tout ce qu’elle possède. \q Il jettera sa puissance dans la mer, \q et la ville sera entièrement brûlée.

es.L: He aquí, el Señor la desposeerá, \q y arrojará al mar su poderío, \q y ella será consumida por el fuego.
es.B: Pero el Señor la despojará de todo lo que tiene \q y hundirá su poder en el mar, \q y ella será devorada por el fuego.
es.R: Pero el Señor le quitará todo lo que tiene. \q Arrojará su poder al mar, \q y la ciudad será quemada hasta los cimientos.

vi.L: Kìa, Chúa sẽ tước đoạt nó, \q và đánh sức mạnh của nó xuống biển, \q và nó sẽ bị lửa thiêu nuốt.
vi.B: Nhưng kìa, Chúa sẽ tước đoạt tất cả những gì nó có, \q và quăng quyền lực của nó xuống biển, \q còn nó sẽ bị lửa thiêu rụi.
vi.R: Nhưng Chúa sẽ lấy đi mọi thứ nó có. \q Ngài sẽ ném quyền lực của nó xuống biển, \q và thành ấy sẽ bị thiêu rụi.

sw.L: Tazama, Bwana atamnyang'anya mali yake \q na kuipiga nguvu yake ndani ya bahari, \q naye ataliwa na moto.
sw.B: Lakini tazama, Bwana atamvua vyote alivyo navyo \q na kuitupa nguvu yake chini baharini, \q naye atateketezwa kwa moto.
sw.R: Lakini Bwana atachukua kila kitu anachomiliki. \q Ataitupa nguvu yake baharini, \q nao mji utateketezwa kabisa kwa moto.

ko.L: 보라, 주님께서 그 성을 빼앗으시고 \q 그 힘을 바다에 쳐 넣으실 것이니, \q 그 성은 불에 삼켜질 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 보아라, 주님께서 그 성이 가진 모든 것을 빼앗으시고 \q 그 힘을 바다에 던져 넣으실 것이다. \q 그 성은 불에 타 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 주님께서 두로가 가진 모든 것을 빼앗으실 것이다. \q 그 힘을 바다에 던져 버리실 것이다. \q 그 성은 불에 타서 무너질 것이다.

pt.L: Eis que o Senhor a despojará \q e lançará no mar o seu poderio, \q e ela será consumida pelo fogo.
pt.B: Mas vejam: o Senhor tomará tudo o que ela tem \q e lançará o seu poder no fundo do mar, \q e ela será queimada pelo fogo.
pt.R: Mas o Senhor vai tirar tudo o que ela tem. \q Ele vai jogar o poder dela no mar, \q e a cidade vai ser queimada até o chão.

decisions.choice: dispossess her: take away all she possesses
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for taking possession of a land and driving out those who held it. Here the Lord takes from Tyre the wealth of verse 3. The city that trusted in its walls and its riches will lose both.

decisions.choice: strike her strength into the sea: destroy her power, which was on the sea
alternatives: strike her rampart into the sea
strike her wealth into the sea
decisions.reason: The noun can mean strength, wealth or an army; a similar word means a rampart. Tyre's power, its wealth and its walls all stood on the sea, and the Lord will throw it down into the sea. Ezekiel 26:12 and 27:27 picture Tyre's wealth sinking into the sea. Read as "rampart", the line pictures the city's sea wall struck down into the water; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: she will be consumed by fire: the burning of a captured city
decisions.reason: A conquered city was burned (Amos 1:10 says the same of Tyre). Tyre was finally taken by storm and burned by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, after he built a causeway out to the island; many readers see that event here. The oracle does not name the conqueror: it is the Lord who acts.

decisions.choice: But look (B); But (R); strip her of all she has (B); take away everything she owns (R); hurl her power down (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "but" to mark the turn from Tyre's pride in verse 3 to its fall. They spell out "dispossess" (m1), and say "power" for "strength" (m2). Readable says "the city" for "she".

decisions.choice: "el Señor"
decisions.reason: Adonai alone is "el Señor", without a divine_name span, as the English "the Lord".

decisions.choice: "주님" for Adonai
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew has Adonai alone it is "주님", kept apart from the divine-name span (term sheet).

decisions.choice: 'Adonai is "Chúa", not in capitals and with no span
decisions.reason: The term sheet's rule: Adonai is plain "Chúa"; only YHWH takes the divine_name span.

source.text: תֵּרֶ֨א אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וְתִירָ֗א וְעַזָּה֙ וְתָחִ֣יל מְאֹ֔ד וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּֽי־הֹבִ֣ישׁ מֶבָּטָ֑הּ וְאָ֤בַד מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ מֵֽעַזָּ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Will see Ashkelon and be afraid, and Gaza, and will writhe greatly, and Ekron, for is put to shame her hope; and will perish a king from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.

en.L: Ashkelon will see [it] and be afraid, and Gaza [will] writhe greatly, \q and Ekron, for her hope has been put to shame; \q and a king will perish from Gaza, \q and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
en.B: Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza will twist in pain, \q and Ekron too, for what she trusted in has failed. \q Gaza will lose her king, \q and Ashkelon will be left empty.
en.R: The people of Ashkelon will see it and be terrified. Gaza will shake with fear, \q and so will Ekron, because what it trusted in has failed. \q Gaza will have no king any longer, \q and no one will live in Ashkelon.

fr.L: Ashqelôn [le] verra et aura peur, et Gaza [se] tordra violemment, \q et Eqrôn, car son espérance a été confondue ; \q et le roi disparaîtra de Gaza, \q et Ashqelôn ne sera plus habitée.
fr.B: Ashqelôn le verra et prendra peur ; Gaza se tordra de douleur, \q et Eqrôn aussi, car ce en quoi elle espérait l’a déçue. \q Gaza perdra son roi, \q et Ashqelôn restera vide.
fr.R: Les habitants d’Ashqelôn le verront et seront terrifiés. Gaza tremblera de peur, \q et Eqrôn aussi, parce que ce en quoi elle avait confiance l’a laissée tomber. \q Gaza n’aura plus de roi, \q et plus personne n’habitera à Ashqelôn.

es.L: Ascalón [lo] verá y temerá, y Gaza se retorcerá de dolor, \q y Ecrón, porque su esperanza ha sido avergonzada; \q y perecerá el rey de Gaza, \q y Ascalón no será habitada.
es.B: Ascalón lo verá y tendrá miedo; Gaza se retorcerá de dolor, \q y también Ecrón, porque le falló aquello en que confiaba. \q Gaza se quedará sin rey, \q y Ascalón quedará deshabitada.
es.R: La gente de Ascalón lo verá y se llenará de terror. Gaza temblará de miedo, \q y lo mismo Ecrón, porque le falló aquello en que confiaba. \q Gaza ya no tendrá rey, \q y nadie vivirá en Ascalón.

vi.L: Ách-ca-lôn sẽ thấy [điều đó] và sợ hãi, Ga-xa [sẽ] quằn quại đau đớn, \q và Éc-rôn, vì niềm hy vọng của nó đã bị hổ thẹn; \q vua sẽ bị diệt khỏi Ga-xa, \q và Ách-ca-lôn sẽ không còn người ở.
vi.B: Ách-ca-lôn sẽ thấy và sợ hãi; Ga-xa sẽ quằn quại đau đớn, \q Éc-rôn cũng vậy, vì điều nó trông cậy đã sụp đổ. \q Ga-xa sẽ mất vua, \q và Ách-ca-lôn sẽ bị bỏ hoang.
vi.R: Dân Ách-ca-lôn sẽ thấy và kinh hãi. Ga-xa sẽ run rẩy vì sợ, \q Éc-rôn cũng vậy, vì điều nó trông cậy đã thất bại. \q Ga-xa sẽ không còn vua nữa, \q và sẽ không còn ai sống ở Ách-ca-lôn.

sw.L: Ashkeloni utaona [hayo] na kuogopa, na Gaza [utagaagaa] kwa maumivu makali, \q na Ekroni, kwa maana tumaini lake limeaibishwa; \q na mfalme atapotea kutoka Gaza, \q na Ashkeloni hautakaliwa na watu.
sw.B: Ashkeloni utaona hayo na kuogopa; Gaza utagaagaa kwa maumivu, \q na Ekroni pia, kwa maana kile alichokitumainia kimeshindwa. \q Gaza utampoteza mfalme wake, \q na Ashkeloni utabaki bila watu.
sw.R: Watu wa Ashkeloni wataona hayo na kuogopa sana. Gaza utatetemeka kwa hofu, \q na Ekroni vilevile, kwa sababu kile walichotumainia kimeshindwa. \q Gaza hautakuwa na mfalme tena, \q na hakuna atakayeishi Ashkeloni.

ko.L: 아스글론이 보고 두려워하고, 가사도 [보고] 몹시 몸부림칠 것이며, \q 에그론도 그러할 것이니, 그 소망이 부끄러움을 당했기 때문이다. \q 가사에서 왕이 끊어지고, \q 아스글론에는 사람이 살지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 아스글론이 그것을 보고 두려워하고, 가사가 고통으로 몸부림칠 것이다. \q 에그론도 그러할 것이니, 믿고 바라던 것이 무너졌기 때문이다. \q 가사에서는 왕이 사라지고, \q 아스글론은 텅 비게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 아스글론 사람들이 그것을 보고 겁에 질릴 것이다. 가사는 두려워 떨 것이다. \q 에그론도 그러할 것이다. 믿고 바라던 것이 무너졌기 때문이다. \q 가사에는 더 이상 왕이 없을 것이다. \q 아스글론에는 아무도 살지 않을 것이다.

pt.L: Asquelom verá [isso] e temerá, e Gaza se contorcerá muito, \q e Ecrom, porque a sua esperança foi envergonhada; \q e o rei perecerá de Gaza, \q e Asquelom não será habitada.
pt.B: Asquelom verá isso e ficará com medo; Gaza se contorcerá de dor, \q e Ecrom também, porque aquilo em que confiava falhou. \q Gaza perderá o seu rei, \q e Asquelom ficará vazia.
pt.R: O povo de Asquelom vai ver isso e ficar apavorado. Gaza vai tremer de medo, \q e Ecrom também, porque aquilo em que confiava falhou. \q Gaza não vai ter mais rei, \q e ninguém vai morar em Asquelom.

decisions.choice: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron (and Ashdod in verse 6): four cities of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines lived on the southern coastal plain, in five chief cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath (1 Samuel 6:17). Gath is missing here, as it is in the oracles against the Philistines in Amos 1:6-8, Jeremiah 25:20 and Zephaniah 2:4; it had probably lost its importance long before.

decisions.choice: her hope has been put to shame: what Ekron trusted in has let her down
decisions.reason: The noun means the thing one looks to with hope or confidence. The Philistine cities had looked to the strength of Tyre and the north to hold back the danger. When Tyre falls (verse 4), they see that their hope was empty, and they are put to shame.

decisions.choice: a king will perish from Gaza; Ashkelon will not be inhabited: the cities will lose their rulers and their people
decisions.reason: A city without its king has lost its independence; a city without inhabitants has been destroyed. Amos 1:8 uses the same pair of pictures of Ashdod and Ashkelon.

decisions.choice: twist in pain (B); shake with fear (R); left empty (B); no one will live (R)
decisions.reason: The verb "writhe" is used of a woman in labor and of shaking with fear; Balanced keeps the picture of pain, Readable gives the sense. Readable speaks of the people of the cities, who are the ones afraid.

decisions.choice: Ashqelôn, Gaza, Eqrôn, Ashdod
decisions.reason: The Philistine cities as the term sheet's names, feminine as cities.

decisions.choice: "Ascalón", "Gaza", "Ecrón"
decisions.reason: The Philistine cities keep their published Spanish forms (1 Samuel 6:17).

decisions.choice: Asquelom, Gaza, Ecrom (and Asdode, verse 6)
decisions.reason: The Philistine cities (m1) take the forms the shared rules for the prophets set in Portuguese, as Amos 1:6-8 and Zephaniah 2:4 have them.

source.text: וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּא֥וֹן פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And will dwell a mixed people in Ashdod, and I will cut off [the] pride of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And a mixed people will dwell in Ashdod, \q and I will cut off the Philistines' pride.
en.B: A people of mixed birth will settle in Ashdod, \q and I will cut down the pride of the Philistines.
en.R: People from many nations will settle in Ashdod. \q I will put an end to the pride of the Philistines.

fr.L: Et un peuple bâtard habitera dans Ashdod, \q et je retrancherai l’orgueil des Philistins.
fr.B: Un peuple d’origine mêlée s’installera à Ashdod, \q et j’abattrai l’orgueil des Philistins.
fr.R: Des gens de toutes sortes de nations s’installeront à Ashdod. \q Je mettrai fin à l’orgueil des Philistins.

es.L: Y un pueblo mestizo habitará en Asdod, \q y cortaré el orgullo de los filisteos.
es.B: Gente de origen mezclado se establecerá en Asdod, \q y abatiré el orgullo de los filisteos.
es.R: Gente de muchas naciones se establecerá en Asdod. \q Acabaré con el orgullo de los filisteos.

vi.L: Một dân lai tạp sẽ ở tại Ách-đốt, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Một dân lai tạp sẽ định cư tại Ách-đốt, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hạ sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Người từ nhiều nước sẽ đến định cư ở Ách-đốt. \q Ta sẽ chấm dứt sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.

sw.L: Na watu wa mchanganyiko watakaa Ashdodi, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakatilia mbali kiburi cha Wafilisti.
sw.B: Watu wa asili iliyochanganyika watakaa Ashdodi, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakiangusha kiburi cha Wafilisti.
sw.R: Watu kutoka mataifa mengi watakaa Ashdodi. \q Nitakikomesha kiburi cha Wafilisti.

ko.L: 혼혈 민족이 아스돗에 살 것이니, \q 내가 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 끊어 버리겠다.
ko.B: 잡족이 아스돗에 자리 잡을 것이다. \q 내가 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 꺾어 버리겠다.
ko.R: 여러 민족에서 온 사람들이 아스돗에 자리 잡을 것이다. \q 나는 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 끝내 버리겠다.

pt.L: E um povo mestiço habitará em Asdode, \q e eliminarei o orgulho dos filisteus.
pt.B: Uma gente de origem misturada se instalará em Asdode, \q e eu abaterei o orgulho dos filisteus.
pt.R: Pessoas de muitas nações vão morar em Asdode. \q Vou acabar com o orgulho dos filisteus.

decisions.choice: a mixed people: people of mixed or doubtful descent
alternatives: a person of illegitimate birth (as Deuteronomy 23:3)
decisions.reason: The word appears elsewhere only in Deuteronomy 23:3, where it describes someone born of a forbidden union, who may not enter the assembly of the LORD. Here it seems to mean a mixed population of foreigners settled in Ashdod in place of its own people, as conquerors often moved peoples from land to land (2 Kings 17:24). The Philistines would no longer be a people of their own.

decisions.choice: I will cut off: the LORD now speaks in his own voice
decisions.reason: Verses 1-5 speak of the LORD in the third person. From here to verse 8 the LORD himself speaks: he is the one who brings down the Philistines' pride, and he will guard his house.

decisions.choice: People from many nations (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "a mixed people" (m1) without the hard edge of the Hebrew word, which it cannot carry plainly.

decisions.choice: "un peuple bâtard" (L), "d'origine mêlée" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word points to doubtful birth, which "bâtard" keeps at Literal; Balanced says it without contempt.

decisions.choice: "un pueblo mestizo" (L); "gente de origen mezclado" (B)
decisions.reason: The word means people of mixed or doubtful descent; Spanish L uses one word for it, B a phrase.

decisions.choice: God speaks in 해라체 with "내가" ("끊어 버리겠다")
decisions.reason: Here the LORD begins to speak in his own voice (meaning decision); God's first-person speech is 해라체 and never takes -시- (term sheet).

source.text: וַהֲסִרֹתִ֨י דָמָ֜יו מִפִּ֗יו וְשִׁקֻּצָיו֙ מִבֵּ֣ין שִׁנָּ֔יו וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר גַּם־ה֖וּא לֵֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהָיָה֙ כְּאַלֻּ֣ף בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּיבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will remove his blood from his mouth, and his detestable things from between his teeth; and will be left also he for our God, and he will be like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like [the] Jebusite.

en.L: And I will remove its blood from its mouth, and its detestable things from between its teeth; \q and it too will be a remnant for our God, \q and it will be like a clan in Judah, \q and Ekron like the Jebusite.
en.B: I will take the blood out of their mouths and the forbidden food from between their teeth. \q Those who are left will belong to our God; \q they will become one of the clans of Judah, \q and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
en.R: I will take away the meat with blood still in it from their mouths, and the unclean food from between their teeth. \q Those who are left will belong to our God. \q They will be like a family group in Judah. \q Ekron will become part of God's people, as the Jebusites did.

fr.L: Et j’ôterai son sang de sa bouche, et ses abominations d’entre ses dents ; \q et lui aussi restera pour notre Dieu, \q et il sera comme un clan en Juda, \q et Eqrôn comme le Jébusien.
fr.B: J’ôterai le sang de leur bouche et la nourriture interdite d’entre leurs dents. \q Ceux qui resteront appartiendront à notre Dieu ; \q ils deviendront comme l’un des clans de Juda, \q et Eqrôn sera comme les Jébusiens.
fr.R: Je leur enlèverai de la bouche la viande avec le sang encore dedans, et d’entre les dents la nourriture impure. \q Ceux qui resteront appartiendront à notre Dieu. \q Ils seront comme une famille de Juda. \q Eqrôn fera partie du peuple de Dieu, comme les Jébusiens autrefois.

es.L: Y quitaré su sangre de su boca, y sus abominaciones de entre sus dientes; \q y también él quedará como remanente para nuestro Dios, \q y será como un clan en Judá, \q y Ecrón como el jebuseo.
es.B: Les quitaré de la boca la sangre y de entre los dientes la comida prohibida. \q Los que queden pertenecerán a nuestro Dios; \q serán como uno de los clanes de Judá, \q y Ecrón será como los jebuseos.
es.R: Les quitaré de la boca la carne que todavía tiene sangre, y de entre los dientes la comida impura. \q Los que queden pertenecerán a nuestro Dios. \q Serán como una familia más de Judá. \q Ecrón llegará a ser parte del pueblo de Dios, como pasó con los jebuseos.

vi.L: Ta sẽ cất máu khỏi miệng nó, và những vật gớm ghiếc khỏi giữa răng nó; \q rồi nó cũng sẽ là phần sót lại cho Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta, \q nó sẽ như một gia tộc trong Giu-đa, \q và Éc-rôn như người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.B: Ta sẽ lấy máu khỏi miệng chúng và thức ăn ô uế khỏi giữa răng chúng. \q Những người còn sót lại sẽ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta; \q họ sẽ trở thành một trong các gia tộc của Giu-đa, \q và Éc-rôn sẽ như người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.R: Ta sẽ lấy thịt còn máu khỏi miệng chúng, và thức ăn ô uế khỏi giữa răng chúng. \q Những người còn sót lại sẽ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta. \q Họ sẽ như một gia tộc trong Giu-đa. \q Éc-rôn sẽ trở thành một phần của dân Đức Chúa Trời, như người Giê-bu-sít ngày xưa.

sw.L: Nami nitaiondoa damu yake kinywani mwake, na vitu vyake vya kuchukiza kutoka kati ya meno yake; \q naye pia atakuwa mabaki kwa ajili ya Mungu wetu, \q naye atakuwa kama ukoo katika Yuda, \q na Ekroni kama Myebusi.
sw.B: Nitaiondoa damu vinywani mwao na vyakula vilivyokatazwa kutoka kati ya meno yao. \q Wale watakaobaki watakuwa mali ya Mungu wetu; \q watakuwa mojawapo ya koo za Yuda, \q na Ekroni atakuwa kama Wayebusi.
sw.R: Nitaiondoa vinywani mwao nyama yenye damu bado ndani yake, na chakula kichafu kutoka kati ya meno yao. \q Wale watakaobaki watakuwa mali ya Mungu wetu. \q Watakuwa kama jamaa moja katika Yuda. \q Ekroni atakuwa sehemu ya watu wa Mungu, kama Wayebusi walivyokuwa.

ko.L: 내가 그 입에서 그 피를, 그 이 사이에서 그 혐오스러운 것들을 없애겠다. \q 그도 우리 하나님께 남은 자가 되어, \q 유다의 한 족속처럼 되고, \q 에그론은 여부스 사람처럼 될 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들의 입에서 피를 없애고, 그들의 이 사이에서 금지된 음식을 없애겠다. \q 남은 사람들은 우리 하나님께 속하여, \q 유다의 한 가문처럼 되고, \q 에그론은 여부스 사람들처럼 될 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 그들의 입에서 피가 그대로 있는 고기를 없애고, 그들의 이 사이에서 부정한 음식을 없애겠다. \q 살아남은 사람들은 우리 하나님께 속할 것이다. \q 그들은 유다의 한 집안처럼 될 것이다. \q 에그론도 여부스 사람들처럼 하나님의 백성이 될 것이다.

pt.L: E removerei o seu sangue da sua boca, e as suas abominações de entre os seus dentes; \q e também ele será um remanescente para o nosso Deus, \q e será como um clã em Judá, \q e Ecrom, como o jebuseu.
pt.B: Tirarei o sangue da boca deles e a comida proibida de entre os seus dentes. \q Os que restarem pertencerão ao nosso Deus; \q eles se tornarão um dos clãs de Judá, \q e Ecrom será como os jebuseus.
pt.R: Vou tirar da boca deles a carne que ainda tem sangue, e de entre os seus dentes a comida impura. \q Os que restarem vão pertencer ao nosso Deus. \q Eles vão ser como uma família de Judá. \q Ecrom vai fazer parte do povo de Deus, como os jebuseus fizeram.

decisions.choice: the blood and the detestable things: meat eaten with its blood, and unclean food from pagan worship
decisions.reason: The law forbade eating meat with its blood still in it (Leviticus 17:10-14) and named foods that were unclean (Leviticus 11). The "detestable things" are such food, probably eaten in the sacrifices of pagan worship, as in Isaiah 65:4 and 66:17. The LORD will take these from the Philistines' mouths: they will no longer worship as they did. The Hebrew speaks of the Philistines as one person ("his mouth", "his teeth").

decisions.choice: it too will be a remnant for our God: some of the Philistines will be brought into God's people
decisions.reason: The judgment of verses 5-6 is not the end. A remnant will be left, the word used for the survivors of Israel (Isaiah 10:20-22), and it will belong to "our God". Those who were Israel's enemies will be counted with Judah. Isaiah 19:23-25 speaks in the same way of Egypt and Assyria. With "our God" the prophet speaks for a moment in his own voice.

decisions.choice: like a clan in Judah: like one of Judah's own families
decisions.reason: The word can mean a clan or the chief of a clan; Genesis 36:15-43 uses it for the chiefs of Edom. Here it most likely means that the Philistine remnant will have a place among the clans of Judah, as a clan or as its leader.

decisions.choice: like the Jebusite: like the people of Jerusalem before David, who were taken into Israel
decisions.reason: The Jebusites held Jerusalem until David captured it (2 Samuel 5:6-9). They were not wiped out but lived on among Israel (Joshua 15:63); Araunah the Jebusite sold David the threshing floor where the temple was built (2 Samuel 24:18-25). Ekron will be taken in the same way.

decisions.choice: their mouths ... their teeth; those who are left (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the Philistines as one person, which Literal keeps with "its". Balanced and Readable use "their" and "those who are left", so that the reader can follow who is meant.

decisions.choice: meat with blood still in it; unclean food; Ekron will become part of God's people, as the Jebusites did (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the blood and the detestable things (m1) and what it means for Ekron to be like the Jebusites (m4).

decisions.choice: "ses abominations" (L), "la nourriture interdite" (B), "la nourriture impure" (R) for shiqqutsim
decisions.reason: Here the word means unclean food from pagan worship, as the meaning decision says, so Balanced and Readable name the food.

decisions.choice: "abominaciones"
decisions.reason: The word is shiqqutsim, detestable things; here it is food from pagan worship, so L uses "abominaciones" in its plain sense and B and R say "comida prohibida" / "impura". It is not the Ezekiel term for idols.

decisions.choice: "el jebuseo" (L); "los jebuseos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Jebusite follows the Spanish of 1 Chronicles 1:14 and 11:4.

decisions.choice: "vitu vyake vya kuchukiza" (L) for shiqqutsim
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps shiqqutsim at Literal as "vitu vya kuchukiza", apart from "machukizo" (to'evah). Here it is unclean food, which Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: "mabaki" (L, as the term sheet); "wale watakaobaki" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "be left" is the remnant root; Balanced and Readable say it with a clause, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "금지된 음식" (B); "부정한 음식" (R); "혐오스러운 것들" (L)
decisions.reason: The detestable things are unclean food from pagan worship (meaning decision); Literal keeps the term sheet's word for shiqqutsim.

decisions.choice: "chúng" for the Philistines under judgment, then "họ" for those brought into God's people
decisions.reason: The term sheet: "chúng" for enemies in the oracles, "họ" in promises; the verse moves from one to the other.

decisions.choice: o jebuseu (L), os jebuseus (B, R); um clã (L, B), uma família (R); um remanescente
decisions.reason: The Jebusites (m4) are "os jebuseus", as 2 Samuel 5:6 has them in Portuguese; Literal keeps the singular of the Hebrew. "Clã", as the Old Testament terms set it (m3); Readable says "família".

source.text: וְחָנִ֨יתִי לְבֵיתִ֤י מִצָּבָה֙ מֵעֹבֵ֣ר וּמִשָּׁ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹד נֹגֵ֑שׂ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will encamp at my house [as] a guard, from [one who] passes and from [one who] returns; and will not pass over them again an oppressor, for now I have seen with my eyes.

en.L: And I will encamp at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house [as] a guard against [any] who pass through and return; \q and no oppressor will pass over them again, \q for now I have seen with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.
en.B: I will camp around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house to guard it from those who march back and forth. \q No oppressor will overrun them again, \q for now I am watching with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own eyes.
en.R: I will set up camp around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house to guard it, so that no army can march through it. \q No cruel ruler will ever again overrun {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q because now I am watching over them {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

fr.L: Et je camperai près de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison [comme] garde contre [ceux qui] passent et reviennent ; \q et l’oppresseur ne passera plus sur eux, \q car maintenant j’ai vu de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux.
fr.B: Je camperai autour de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison pour la garder contre ceux qui vont et viennent. \q Aucun oppresseur ne les envahira plus, \q car maintenant je veille de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} propres yeux.
fr.R: J’installerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} camp autour de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison pour la garder, et aucune armée ne pourra la traverser. \q Aucun chef cruel n’envahira plus jamais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q car maintenant je veille {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} sur lui.

es.L: Y acamparé junto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa [como] guardia contra [todo] el que pase y vuelva; \q y no pasará más sobre ellos el opresor, \q porque ahora he visto con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos.
es.B: Acamparé alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa para protegerla de los que van y vienen. \q Ningún opresor volverá a invadirlos, \q porque ahora yo vigilo con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} propios ojos.
es.R: Pondré mi campamento alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa para protegerla, y ningún ejército podrá pasar por ella. \q Ningún gobernante cruel volverá a invadir a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q porque ahora yo {{deity_pronoun:mismo|Mismo}} lo estoy cuidando.

vi.L: Ta sẽ đóng trại nơi nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [làm] lính canh, chống lại [kẻ] đi qua và [kẻ] trở lại; \q kẻ áp bức sẽ không còn đi qua trên chúng nữa, \q vì nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy tận mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ta sẽ đóng trại quanh nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để canh giữ nó khỏi những kẻ kéo quân qua lại. \q Kẻ áp bức sẽ không còn giày xéo họ nữa, \q vì nay chính mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang canh chừng.
vi.R: Ta sẽ đóng trại quanh nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để canh giữ, không cho đạo quân nào kéo qua. \q Sẽ không còn kẻ cai trị độc ác nào giày xéo dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nữa, \q vì bây giờ chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang trông chừng họ.

sw.L: Nami nitapiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [kama] mlinzi dhidi ya [wale] wanaopita na kurudi; \q wala mdhalimu hatapita juu yao tena, \q kwa maana sasa nimeona kwa macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Nitapiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ili kuilinda dhidi ya wale wanaopita huku na huko. \q Hakuna mdhalimu atakayewashambulia tena, \q kwa maana sasa ninaangalia kwa macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.
sw.R: Nitaweka kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ili kuilinda, ili jeshi lolote lisiweze kupita ndani yake. \q Hakuna mtawala mkatili atakayewashambulia tena watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q kwa sababu sasa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ninawaangalia.

ko.L: 내가 내 집을 위하여 진을 치고 지켜서, 오가는 자를 막겠다. \q 압제자가 다시는 그들을 지나가지 못할 것이니, \q 이제 내가 내 눈으로 보았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내가 내 집 둘레에 진을 치고, 이리저리 쳐들어오는 자들로부터 그 집을 지키겠다. \q 어떤 압제자도 다시는 그들을 짓밟지 못할 것이다. \q 이제 내가 내 눈으로 지켜보고 있기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 내 성전 둘레에 진을 치고 그곳을 지켜서, 어떤 군대도 그곳을 지나가지 못하게 하겠다. \q 어떤 잔인한 통치자도 다시는 내 백성을 짓밟지 못할 것이다. \q 이제 내가 직접 그들을 지켜보고 있기 때문이다.

pt.L: E acamparei junto à {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} casa [como] guarda contra os que passam e voltam; \q e não passará mais sobre eles um opressor, \q porque agora vi com os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos.
pt.B: Acamparei ao redor da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} casa para protegê-la dos que marcham de um lado para o outro. \q Nenhum opressor os invadirá de novo, \q porque agora estou vigiando com os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} próprios olhos.
pt.R: Vou acampar em volta da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} casa para protegê-la, para que nenhum exército passe por ela. \q Nenhum governante cruel vai invadir de novo o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, \q porque agora eu mesmo estou cuidando dele.

decisions.choice: my house: the LORD's temple, and with it his land and people
decisions.reason: "My house" is the temple in Jerusalem, rebuilt in Zechariah's day (1:16; 4:9). Hosea uses "the house of the LORD" for the land and people of Israel as well (Hosea 8:1; 9:15). The next line, "over them", shows that the LORD guards the people, not only the building.

decisions.choice: as a guard, against any who pass through and return: protection from marching armies
alternatives: against an army, against any who pass through and return
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a word that may be read "against an army" or "as a guard"; the difference is one letter, and the sense is the same. "Those who pass through and return" are armies marching back and forth across the land, as the armies of Egypt and of the northern empires had done for centuries.

decisions.choice: now I have seen with my eyes: the LORD has taken notice and will act
decisions.reason: When the LORD "sees" his people's suffering, he acts to help them, as in Exodus 3:7: "I have surely seen the affliction of my people". The oppression is now in his sight, and he will not let it go on.

decisions.choice: no army can march through it; my people; watching over them myself (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are and what "seen with my eyes" means (m3). The pronouns for the LORD take the deity_pronoun setting, since the LORD is speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: "yo mismo"
decisions.reason: The English R's "myself" takes a deity_pronoun span; Spanish puts it on "mismo", the free word that carries it.

source.text: גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֨יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה מַלְכֵּךְ֙ יָ֣בוֹא לָ֔ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְנוֹשָׁ֖ע ה֑וּא עָנִי֙ וְרֹכֵ֣ב עַל־חֲמ֔וֹר וְעַל־עַ֖יִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you; righteous and saved [is] he, humble and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, [the] son of female donkeys.

en.L: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem! \q Look, your king comes to you; \q righteous and victorious [is] he, \q humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
en.B: Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout aloud, Daughter Jerusalem! \q Look, your king is coming to you; \q righteous and victorious is he, \q humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
en.R: Be very glad, people of Zion! Shout for joy, people of Jerusalem! \q Look, your king is coming to you. \q He does what is right, and he has won the victory. \q He comes humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

fr.L: Réjouis-toi grandement, fille de Sion ! Pousse des cris, fille de Jérusalem ! \q Voici, ton roi vient à toi ; \q juste et victorieux, il [est] \q humble et monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.
fr.B: Sois transportée de joie, fille de Sion ! Lance des cris, fille de Jérusalem ! \q Voici que ton roi vient à toi ; \q il est juste et victorieux, \q humble et monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.
fr.R: Sois très heureux, peuple de Sion ! Crie de joie, peuple de Jérusalem ! \q Regarde, ton roi vient à toi. \q Il fait ce qui est juste, et il a remporté la victoire. \q Il vient humble et monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.

es.L: ¡Alégrate mucho, hija de Sion! ¡Grita de júbilo, hija de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey viene a ti; \q justo y victorioso [es] él, \q humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.
es.B: ¡Llénate de alegría, hija de Sion! ¡Grita de júbilo, hija de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey viene hacia ti; \q es justo y victorioso, \q humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.
es.R: ¡Alégrate mucho, pueblo de Sion! ¡Grita de alegría, gente de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey viene a ti. \q Él hace lo que es justo y ha alcanzado la victoria. \q Viene humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.

vi.L: Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, hãy vui mừng lớn tiếng! Hỡi con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của ngươi đến với ngươi; \q người là công chính và chiến thắng, \q khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.
vi.B: Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, hãy vui mừng lớn tiếng! Hỡi con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của ngươi đang đến với ngươi; \q người công chính và đắc thắng, \q khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Si-ôn, hãy hết sức vui mừng! Hỡi dân Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của các ngươi đang đến với các ngươi. \q Người làm điều công chính, và người đã chiến thắng. \q Người đến khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.

sw.L: Furahi sana, binti Sayuni! Piga kelele kwa shangwe, binti Yerusalemu! \q Tazama, mfalme wako anakujia; \q yeye [ni] mwenye haki na mshindi, \q mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.
sw.B: Furahi sana, Binti Sayuni! Piga kelele kwa shangwe, Binti Yerusalemu! \q Tazama, mfalme wako anakujia; \q yeye ni mwenye haki na mshindi, \q mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.
sw.R: Furahini sana, enyi watu wa Sayuni! Pigeni kelele kwa shangwe, enyi watu wa Yerusalemu! \q Tazameni, mfalme wenu anakuja kwenu. \q Yeye hutenda yaliyo haki, naye ameshinda. \q Anakuja mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.

ko.L: 딸 시온아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 딸 예루살렘아, 소리 높여 외쳐라! \q 보라, 네 왕이 네게 온다. \q 그는 의롭고 승리를 얻었으며, \q 겸손하여 나귀를, \q 나귀 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 있다.
ko.B: 딸 시온아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 딸 예루살렘아, 소리 높여 외쳐라! \q 보아라, 네 왕이 너에게 온다. \q 그는 의롭고 승리를 얻었으며, \q 겸손하여 나귀를, \q 나귀 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 있다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 예루살렘 백성아, 기뻐 외쳐라! \q 보아라, 너희 왕이 너희에게 온다. \q 그는 옳은 일을 하고, 승리를 얻었다. \q 그는 겸손하여 나귀를 타고 온다. \q 나귀 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 온다.

pt.L: Alegra-te muito, filha de Sião! Grita, filha de Jerusalém! \q Eis que o teu rei vem a ti; \q justo e vitorioso [é] ele, \q humilde e montado num jumento, \q num jumentinho, cria de uma jumenta.
pt.B: Alegra-te muito, filha de Sião! Grita de alegria, filha de Jerusalém! \q Olha, o teu rei está vindo a ti; \q ele é justo e vitorioso, \q humilde e montado num jumento, \q num jumentinho, cria de uma jumenta.
pt.R: Fiquem muito alegres, povo de Sião! Gritem de alegria, povo de Jerusalém! \q Vejam! O seu rei está vindo até vocês. \q Ele faz o que é justo e conquistou a vitória. \q Ele vem humilde e montado num jumento, \q num jumentinho, cria de uma jumenta.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion, daughter of Jerusalem: the city and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and stands for the city. The prophets picture the city and its people as a young woman, loved and called to rejoice (Isaiah 62:11; Zephaniah 3:14). The two names say the same thing twice, as Hebrew poetry does.

decisions.choice: righteous and victorious: a just king to whom God has given the victory
alternatives: righteous and bringing salvation (following the Septuagint)
decisions.reason: "Righteous" means that the king rules justly and is in the right before God, as the promised king of David's line will be (Isaiah 9:6; 11:4-5; Jeremiah 23:5). The second word is a passive form of the verb "save": "saved" or "delivered", that is, one whom God has rescued and given victory, as in Psalm 33:16, "a king is not saved by a great army". He does not win by his own strength. The Septuagint reads "saving", a king who saves others.

decisions.choice: humble: lowly, afflicted, not proud
decisions.reason: The word means poor or afflicted, and so humble, the opposite of the proud. It is used of those who suffer and depend on God (Psalm 18:28; Zephaniah 3:12). Matthew 21:5 follows the Greek, which has "gentle".

decisions.choice: riding on a donkey, on a colt: a king who comes in peace, not on a war horse
decisions.reason: Kings rode donkeys and mules in times of peace: David had Solomon ride his own mule to be anointed (1 Kings 1:33), and Genesis 49:11 pictures the ruler from Judah with his donkey's colt. A horse was the animal of war, and verse 10 says that the LORD will take the war horse from Jerusalem. The poem names the animal twice, in parallel, as Hebrew poetry does: "a donkey" and "a colt, the foal of a donkey" are one animal, a young male donkey.

decisions.choice: quoted in Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem
decisions.reason: When Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, Matthew and John say that this verse was fulfilled. Matthew 21:5 opens with words from Isaiah 62:11 ("Say to the daughter of Zion") and follows the Greek ("gentle"). Matthew also tells of two animals, a donkey and her colt (Matthew 21:2-7), where the Hebrew names one animal twice; John 12:14-15 speaks of one young donkey. The verse is translated here from the Hebrew as it stands.

decisions.choice: your king: the promised king who comes to Zion
decisions.reason: Zion had no king of its own in Zechariah's day; Judah was a province of Persia. The verse promises that its king will come, as the prophets promised a king of David's line (Jeremiah 23:5; Micah 5:1-3). The verse does not name him. Christians read it of Jesus, as the Gospels do (m5).

decisions.choice: humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey (every level)
decisions.reason: These words are the same at every level, so that the reader can hear them in the Gospels' quotations. Balanced and Readable say "is coming", and Literal and Balanced keep the order of "righteous and victorious is he" as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: people of Zion, people of Jerusalem; He does what is right, and he has won the victory (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" and "the people of Jerusalem" for "daughter of Zion" and "daughter of Jerusalem", as in Isaiah, and explains "righteous and victorious" (m2).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span for the king
decisions.reason: As with the king of Isaiah 9:6 and 11:1 and the servant of Isaiah 42-53, the pronouns for the king take no deity_pronoun span. The verse speaks of him as a human king, and capital letters would settle a question of interpretation that the text leaves to the reader (m6).

decisions.choice: "fille de Sion" (L, B), "ton roi vient à toi", "un ânon", as the published Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; "humble" for ʿani, not Matthew's "doux"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the shared words are kept so the quotation can be seen, and the Hebrew word, which means lowly, is translated as such; Matthew's "doux" follows the Greek.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span for the king
decisions.reason: As the English and the term sheet; Readable keeps "tu" to the people of Zion, addressed as one.

decisions.choice: "humilde y montado sobre un asno, sobre un pollino, cría de asna" at every level
decisions.reason: The line is kept the same at every level, as the English does, so that Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 can be seen. The Hebrew 'ani is "humilde"; Matthew 21:5 in Spanish has "manso", from the Greek, and two animals.

decisions.choice: "hija de Sion", "hija de Jerusalén" (L, B); "pueblo de Sion", "gente de Jerusalén" (R)
decisions.reason: Daughter Zion follows Isaiah and John 12:15 in Spanish; the city is addressed as one woman with tú at every level. The king takes no deity_pronoun span, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni", "binti Yerusalemu" (L); capitalized (B); "watu wa Sayuni", "watu wa Yerusalemu" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and the published Isaiah and 2 Kings 19:21. Readable addresses the people with plural verbs ("Furahini", "mfalme wenu").

decisions.choice: "mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda" at every level; no deity_pronoun span on the king
decisions.reason: Translated from the Hebrew "'ani" (lowly, humble). Matthew 21:5 in the published Swahili has "mpole", from the Greek of the Septuagint, and speaks of two animals; John 12:15 shortens the line. The king takes no deity_pronoun span, as in English.

decisions.choice: "네 왕이 네게 온다"; "그는"; "겸손하여"; no -시- for the king
decisions.reason: Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 quote this verse of Jesus and say "오신다" with the honorific; here, as the English leaves the king without a deity span, the term sheet keeps him without -시-, and the allusion stays visible in "네 왕이 네게" and the colt. Matthew's "온유하시며" is from the Greek; the Hebrew 'ani is "겸손하여".

decisions.choice: "딸 시온아", "딸 예루살렘아" (L, B); "시온 백성아", "예루살렘 백성아" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for daughter Zion; Readable speaks to the people and so says "너희".

decisions.choice: "Vua của ngươi" (L, B) / "Vua của các ngươi" (R), as Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; "khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái" at every level; "người", lowercase, with no deity span
decisions.reason: The term sheet: the quoted verse's address wins over Isaiah's "con". Matthew 21:5 says "hiền lành" from the Greek and has two animals; the Hebrew has one animal named twice in parallel and the word for humble, afflicted. The king takes no deity span, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Eis que o teu rei vem a ti (L); Olha, o teu rei está vindo a ti (B); Vejam! O seu rei está vindo até vocês (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 quote the verse (m5), so each level keeps their Portuguese where the Hebrew is the same: Matthew's "Eis que o teu rei vem a ti" at Literal, John's "Olha, o teu rei está vindo" at Balanced, and Matthew's "Vejam! O seu rei está vindo até vocês" at Readable, which speaks to "povo de Sião" with "vocês" as the Gospels' Readable does; Literal and Balanced speak to the daughter of Zion as one woman, with "tu" (m1), as Isaiah 1:8 and Zephaniah 3:14 do.

decisions.choice: humilde e montado num jumento, num jumentinho, cria de uma jumenta (every level)
decisions.reason: The line keeps one wording at every level, as the English does (r-en-1). Here the Gospels follow the Greek and the Hebrew differs, so Portuguese follows the Hebrew: "humilde", the lowly and afflicted (m3), where Matthew 21:5 has "manso" from the Greek; "num jumentinho" with no "e" before it, since the Hebrew names one animal twice (m4), where Matthew has "e num jumentinho"; and "cria de uma jumenta", as John 12:15 says, where Matthew has "cria de animal de carga". The king's pronouns take no deity_pronoun span (r-en-3).

source.text: וְהִכְרַתִּי־רֶ֣כֶב מֵאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְסוּס֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנִכְרְתָה֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמָשְׁלוֹ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֔ם וּמִנָּהָ֖ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will cut off chariot from Ephraim, and horse from Jerusalem, and will be cut off [the] bow of battle; and he will speak peace to the nations, and his rule [will be] from sea to sea, and from [the] River to [the] ends of [the] earth.

en.L: And I will cut off chariotry from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem, \q and cut off will be the bow of battle; \q and he will speak peace to the nations; \q his rule [will reach] from sea to sea, \q and from the River to [the] ends of [the] earth.
en.B: I will take away the chariots from Ephraim and the war horses from Jerusalem, \q and the battle bow will be broken. \q He will proclaim peace to the nations; \q his rule will stretch from sea to sea, \q from the River to the far ends of the earth.
en.R: I will take away the war chariots from Israel and the war horses from Jerusalem. \q The bows used in battle will be broken. \q Your king will bring peace to the nations. \q He will rule over all the land between the seas, \q from the Euphrates River to the farthest places on earth.

fr.L: Et je retrancherai les chars d’Éphraïm et les chevaux de Jérusalem, \q et l’arc de guerre sera retranché ; \q et il parlera de paix aux nations ; \q et sa domination [ira] d’une mer à l’autre mer, \q et depuis le Fleuve jusqu’aux extrémités de [la] terre.
fr.B: Je supprimerai les chars d’Éphraïm et les chevaux de guerre de Jérusalem, \q et l’arc de guerre sera brisé. \q Il annoncera la paix aux nations ; \q son pouvoir s’étendra d’une mer à l’autre, \q depuis le Fleuve jusqu’au bout de la terre.
fr.R: Je supprimerai les chars de guerre d’Israël et les chevaux de guerre de Jérusalem. \q Les arcs qui servent à la guerre seront brisés. \q Ton roi apportera la paix aux nations. \q Il régnera sur tout le pays entre les mers, \q depuis le fleuve Euphrate jusqu’aux endroits les plus lointains de la terre.

es.L: Y cortaré el carro de Efraín y el caballo de Jerusalén, \q y será cortado el arco de guerra; \q y él hablará paz a las naciones; \q y su dominio [será] de mar a mar, \q y desde el Río hasta [los] confines de [la] tierra.
es.B: Quitaré los carros de Efraín y los caballos de guerra de Jerusalén, \q y el arco de guerra será quebrado. \q Él anunciará paz a las naciones; \q su dominio se extenderá de mar a mar, \q desde el Río hasta los extremos de la tierra.
es.R: Quitaré los carros de guerra de Israel y los caballos de guerra de Jerusalén. \q Los arcos de la batalla serán quebrados. \q Tu rey traerá la paz a las naciones. \q Gobernará sobre toda la tierra que hay entre los mares, \q desde el río Éufrates hasta los lugares más lejanos de la tierra.

vi.L: Ta sẽ diệt trừ xe chiến mã khỏi Ép-ra-im và ngựa khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q cung chiến trận sẽ bị bẻ gãy; \q người sẽ công bố hòa bình cho các dân tộc; \q quyền cai trị của người [sẽ] từ biển này đến biển kia, \q và từ Sông Cái đến [tận] cùng trái đất.
vi.B: Ta sẽ cất bỏ xe chiến mã khỏi Ép-ra-im và chiến mã khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q cung chiến trận sẽ bị bẻ gãy. \q Người sẽ công bố hòa bình cho các dân tộc; \q quyền cai trị của người sẽ trải từ biển này đến biển kia, \q từ Sông Cái đến tận cùng trái đất.
vi.R: Ta sẽ cất bỏ xe chiến mã khỏi Y-sơ-ra-ên và chiến mã khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem. \q Cung tên dùng trong chiến trận sẽ bị bẻ gãy. \q Vua của các ngươi sẽ đem hòa bình đến cho các dân tộc. \q Người sẽ cai trị cả vùng đất giữa các biển, \q từ sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến những nơi xa nhất trên mặt đất.

sw.L: Nami nitakatilia mbali magari ya vita kutoka Efraimu na farasi kutoka Yerusalemu, \q nao upinde wa vita utakatiliwa mbali; \q naye atasema amani kwa mataifa; \q na utawala wake [utakuwa] kutoka bahari hata bahari, \q na kutoka Mto hata miisho ya dunia.
sw.B: Nitayaondoa magari ya vita kutoka Efraimu na farasi wa vita kutoka Yerusalemu, \q nao upinde wa vita utavunjwa. \q Atayatangazia mataifa amani; \q utawala wake utaenea kutoka bahari hata bahari, \q kutoka Mto hata miisho ya mbali ya dunia.
sw.R: Nitayaondoa magari ya vita kutoka Israeli na farasi wa vita kutoka Yerusalemu. \q Pinde zinazotumiwa vitani zitavunjwa. \q Mfalme wenu ataleta amani kwa mataifa. \q Atatawala nchi yote kati ya bahari, \q kutoka Mto Frati mpaka mahali pa mbali kabisa duniani.

ko.L: 내가 에브라임에서 병거를, 예루살렘에서 말을 끊어 버리고, \q 전쟁의 활도 끊어질 것이다. \q 그가 민족들에게 평화를 말할 것이니, \q 그의 다스림이 바다에서 바다까지, \q 강에서 땅끝까지 [미칠 것이다].
ko.B: 내가 에브라임에서 병거를 없애고 예루살렘에서 군마를 없애겠다. \q 전쟁에 쓰는 활도 꺾일 것이다. \q 그가 민족들에게 평화를 선포할 것이다. \q 그의 다스림이 바다에서 바다까지, \q 그 강에서 땅 끝까지 미칠 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 이스라엘에서 전차를 없애고, 예루살렘에서 전쟁에 쓰는 말을 없애겠다. \q 전쟁에 쓰는 활은 부러질 것이다. \q 너희 왕은 민족들에게 평화를 가져다줄 것이다. \q 그는 바다와 바다 사이의 온 땅을 다스리고, \q 유프라테스 강에서 땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 다스릴 것이다.

pt.L: E eliminarei os carros de Efraim e os cavalos de Jerusalém, \q e o arco de guerra será eliminado; \q e ele falará paz às nações; \q e o seu domínio [irá] de mar a mar, \q e desde o Rio até [os] confins da terra.
pt.B: Tirarei os carros de guerra de Efraim e os cavalos de guerra de Jerusalém, \q e o arco de guerra será quebrado. \q Ele anunciará paz às nações; \q o seu domínio se estenderá de mar a mar, \q desde o Rio até os confins da terra.
pt.R: Vou tirar de Israel os carros de guerra e de Jerusalém os cavalos de guerra. \q Os arcos usados nas batalhas vão ser quebrados. \q O seu rei vai trazer paz para as nações. \q Ele vai governar toda a terra entre os mares, \q desde o rio Eufrates até os lugares mais distantes do mundo.

decisions.choice: I will cut off the chariot, the horse and the bow: the LORD himself ends war
decisions.reason: Chariots, horses and bows were the weapons of war. The LORD takes them away from his own people, from Ephraim (the northern tribes) and Jerusalem alike, so that the king of verse 9 rules without them. Peace comes as the LORD's gift, not by force of arms (Hosea 2:20; Micah 5:9-10; Psalm 46:10). The Septuagint reads "he will cut off", making the king the one who acts.

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Jerusalem: the northern and southern kingdoms, one people again
decisions.reason: Ephraim stands for the northern tribes of Israel, which had been taken into exile by Assyria two centuries before; Jerusalem for Judah. The promise is for all Israel, reunited under one king (10:6; Ezekiel 37:15-22).

decisions.choice: speak peace to the nations: announce peace, and bring it about
decisions.reason: To "speak peace" is to declare an end of hostility and to offer friendship (Esther 9:30; Psalm 85:9). The king's word to the nations is peace, where kings usually spoke war.

decisions.choice: his rule from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth: the words of Psalm 72:8
decisions.reason: The line repeats Psalm 72:8, a prayer for the king of David's line, and is translated with the same words. "The River" is the Euphrates; "from sea to sea" may mean from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean, or simply the whole earth. The king's rule has no limit.

decisions.choice: the wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: The last two lines reuse the published wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level (m4). Readable says "Israel" for Ephraim and "your king" for "he", so that the reader can tell who is meant (m2), and Balanced and Readable say "war horses" and "broken" for the bow.

decisions.choice: The published Psalm 72:8 at each level for "from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth"
decisions.reason: The term sheet asks for the parallel to be reused where the Hebrew is the same; Zechariah has "his rule" (noun) where the Psalm has a verb, so L and B say "sa domination", "son pouvoir".

decisions.choice: the wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: "de mar a mar, y desde el Río hasta [los] confines de [la] tierra" (L), "de mar a mar, desde el Río hasta los extremos de la tierra" (B) and "entre los mares, desde el río Éufrates hasta los lugares más lejanos de la tierra" (R) reuse the published Spanish Psalm, as the English does.

decisions.choice: the published Swahili of Psalm 72:8 at each level for the last two lines
decisions.reason: The two lines are the words of Psalm 72:8; Swahili reuses the published wording ("kutoka bahari hata bahari", "kutoka Mto hata miisho ya dunia"), changing only "atawale" to "utawala wake" where Zechariah has a noun.

decisions.choice: The last two lines reuse the Korean Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: The line quotes Psalm 72:8 (meaning decision), so the published Korean of that verse is reused, turned from a prayer into a statement.

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse the published Vietnamese of Psalm 72:8 at each level ("từ biển này đến biển kia, từ Sông Cái đến tận cùng trái đất"), turned from a wish into a promise
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as Psalm 72:8, so the wording is shared, as the English does; only the psalm's "nguyện" ("may") is dropped.

decisions.choice: the wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: The last two lines (m4) keep the Portuguese of Psalm 72:8 at each level where the Hebrew is the same: "de mar a mar, e desde o Rio até [os] confins da terra" (L), "se estenderá de mar a mar, desde o Rio até os confins da terra" (B), "toda a terra entre os mares, desde o rio Eufrates até os lugares mais distantes do mundo" (R), as the English does (r-en-1). Readable says "Israel" for Ephraim (m2) and "o seu rei" for "he".

source.text: גַּם־אַ֣תְּ בְּדַם־בְּרִיתֵ֗ךְ שִׁלַּ֤חְתִּי אֲסִירַ֨יִךְ֙מִבּ֔וֹר אֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also you, by [the] blood of your covenant, I will send out your prisoners from a pit [in which there is] no water in it.

en.L: You also, because of the blood of your covenant, \q I will set your prisoners free from the pit [that has] no water in it.
en.B: As for you, because of the blood of your covenant, \q I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.
en.R: As for you, people of Zion, I made a covenant with you and sealed it with blood. \q Because of that, I will set your prisoners free from the dry pit.

fr.L: Toi aussi, à cause du sang de ton alliance, \q je libère tes prisonniers de la fosse où il n’y a pas d’eau.
fr.B: Quant à toi, à cause du sang de ton alliance, \q je libérerai tes prisonniers de la fosse sans eau.
fr.R: Peuple de Sion, j’ai fait une alliance avec toi et je l’ai scellée par le sang. \q À cause de cela, je libérerai tes prisonniers de la citerne sèche.

es.L: Y tú también, por la sangre de tu pacto, \q libertaré a tus prisioneros del pozo en el que no [hay] agua.
es.B: En cuanto a ti, por la sangre de tu pacto, \q libertaré a tus prisioneros del pozo sin agua.
es.R: En cuanto a ti, pueblo de Sion, hice un pacto contigo y lo sellé con sangre. \q Por eso libertaré a tus prisioneros del pozo seco.

vi.L: Còn ngươi nữa, vì cớ máu của giao ước ngươi, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thả những tù nhân của ngươi ra khỏi hố không có nước.
vi.B: Còn con, vì cớ máu của giao ước với con, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giải thoát những tù nhân của con khỏi hố cạn nước.
vi.R: Còn các con, hỡi dân Si-ôn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã lập giao ước với các con và đóng ấn bằng máu. \q Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giải thoát những người bị bắt của các con khỏi hố khô cạn.

sw.L: Nawe pia, kwa sababu ya damu ya agano lako, \q nitawatoa wafungwa wako kutoka shimoni [lisilo na] maji ndani yake.
sw.B: Na kwa habari yako, kwa sababu ya damu ya agano lako, \q nitawaweka huru wafungwa wako kutoka katika shimo lisilo na maji.
sw.R: Na ninyi, watu wa Sayuni, nilifanya agano nanyi nikalithibitisha kwa damu. \q Kwa sababu hiyo nitawaweka huru wafungwa wenu kutoka katika shimo lililokauka.

ko.L: 너도, 네 언약의 피 때문에 \q 내가 네 갇힌 자들을 물 없는 구덩이에서 놓아주겠다.
ko.B: 너에게 말한다. 너와 맺은 언약의 피 때문에 \q 내가 네 갇힌 사람들을 물 없는 구덩이에서 풀어 주겠다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 나는 너희와 언약을 맺고 피로 그 언약을 확정했다. \q 그러므로 내가 너희 가운데 갇힌 사람들을 마른 구덩이에서 풀어 주겠다.

pt.L: Também tu, por causa do sangue da tua aliança, \q libertarei os teus prisioneiros da cova onde não há água.
pt.B: Quanto a ti, por causa do sangue da tua aliança, \q libertarei os teus prisioneiros da cova sem água.
pt.R: Quanto a ti, povo de Sião, eu fiz uma aliança contigo e a selei com sangue. \q Por isso vou libertar os teus prisioneiros da cova seca.

decisions.choice: you: Zion, addressed again
decisions.reason: The "you" is feminine singular, so the LORD now speaks to Daughter Zion of verse 9. The prisoners are her own people, still scattered among the nations.

decisions.choice: the blood of your covenant: the covenant made at Sinai and sealed with blood
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses threw the blood of the sacrifices on the people and said, "Look, the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you" (Exodus 24:8). Because of that covenant, the LORD will not leave his people in captivity. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of the cup as "my blood of the covenant" (Matthew 26:28; Mark 14:24).

decisions.choice: the pit with no water in it: a dry cistern used as a prison
decisions.reason: Cisterns cut into the rock held rainwater; an empty one made a prison from which no one could climb out. Joseph's brothers threw him into such a pit (Genesis 37:24), and Jeremiah was let down into one (Jeremiah 38:6). Exile is pictured as such a pit.

decisions.choice: people of Zion; I made a covenant with you and sealed it with blood (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who is spoken to (m1) and explains "the blood of your covenant" (m2) in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "tú", "tus"
decisions.reason: Zion is addressed again as one woman with tú, as the Hebrew is singular.

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B) / "các con" (R, "people of Zion") to Zion in this promise
decisions.reason: The term sheet: God speaks to Zion with "ngươi" at L and "con" at B and R in promises; R speaks to the people, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: tu (God to Zion), at every level; o sangue da tua aliança
decisions.reason: The "you" is feminine singular, Zion (m1), so every level says "tu", Readable included, where it names "povo de Sião" as the English Readable does. "O sangue da aliança" is the phrase of Exodus 24:8 and Matthew 26:28 in Portuguese (m2).

source.text: שׁ֚וּבוּ לְבִצָּר֔וֹן אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־הַיּ֕וֹם מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Return to [the] stronghold, prisoners of the hope; also today [I am] declaring [that] double I will restore to you.

en.L: Return to [the] stronghold, \q prisoners of hope; \q even today I am declaring: \q double I will restore to you.
en.B: Come back to the stronghold, \q you prisoners who have hope! \q Even today I announce \q that I will give back to you double.
en.R: You prisoners who still have hope, \q come back to the place where you will be safe! \q Today I promise you \q that I will give you back twice as much as you lost.

fr.L: Revenez à la forteresse, \q prisonniers de l’espérance ; \q aujourd’hui encore je le déclare : \q je te rendrai le double.
fr.B: Revenez à la forteresse, \q vous, prisonniers pleins d’espérance ! \q Aujourd’hui même je l’annonce : \q je te rendrai le double.
fr.R: Vous, les prisonniers qui avez encore de l’espoir, \q revenez à l’endroit où vous serez en sécurité ! \q Aujourd’hui, je te le promets : \q je te rendrai deux fois plus que ce que tu as perdu.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a la fortaleza, \q prisioneros de la esperanza; \q aun hoy declaro: \q el doble te devolveré.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Regresen|Regresad}} a la fortaleza, \q prisioneros que tienen esperanza! \q Hoy mismo anuncio \q que te devolveré el doble.
es.R: ¡Prisioneros que todavía tienen esperanza, \q {{plural_you:regresen|regresad}} al lugar donde estarán a salvo! \q Hoy {{plural_you:les|os}} prometo \q que {{plural_you:les|os}} devolveré el doble de lo que perdieron.

vi.L: Hãy trở về đồn lũy, \q hỡi những tù nhân của hy vọng; \q ngay hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} công bố: \q Ta sẽ hoàn lại cho ngươi gấp đôi.
vi.B: Hãy trở về đồn lũy, \q hỡi những tù nhân đang có hy vọng! \q Ngay hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} công bố \q rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hoàn lại cho con gấp đôi.
vi.R: Hỡi những người bị bắt mà vẫn còn hy vọng, \q hãy trở về nơi các con sẽ được an toàn! \q Hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hứa với các con \q rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trả lại cho các con gấp đôi những gì các con đã mất.

sw.L: Rudini kwenye ngome, \q enyi wafungwa wa tumaini; \q hata leo ninatangaza: \q nitakurudishia maradufu.
sw.B: Rudini kwenye ngome, \q enyi wafungwa wenye tumaini! \q Hata leo ninatangaza \q kwamba nitakurudishia maradufu.
sw.R: Enyi wafungwa ambao bado mna tumaini, \q rudini mahali mtakapokuwa salama! \q Leo ninawaahidi \q kwamba nitawarudishia mara mbili ya kile mlichopoteza.

ko.L: 요새로 돌아오너라, \q 소망을 품은 갇힌 자들아. \q 오늘도 내가 선언한다. \q 내가 너에게 갑절로 갚아 주겠다.
ko.B: 요새로 돌아오너라, \q 소망을 품은 갇힌 사람들아! \q 오늘 내가 선언한다. \q 내가 너에게 갑절로 돌려주겠다.
ko.R: 아직 소망을 품고 있는 갇힌 사람들아, \q 안전한 곳으로 돌아오너라! \q 오늘 내가 너희에게 약속한다. \q 너희가 잃은 것의 두 배로 돌려주겠다.
